## gitshift discover

Auto-discover existing Git accounts on your system

### Synopsis

Automatically discover and import existing Git accounts from:

- Every authenticated GitHub CLI account on every configured host
- SSH keys in ~/.ssh/ directory
- GPG signing keys from system keyring
- Matches provider, SSH, and GPG evidence only when email ownership is unambiguous

GitHub CLI identities are keyed by provider, hostname, and username, so multiple
accounts on github.com and GitHub Enterprise hosts remain separate. Discovery
does not switch the active GitHub CLI account or store provider tokens.

On a fresh interactive installation, discovery asks for aliases and which
account to activate, then applies that account. Redirected and later discovery
runs retain non-interactive import behavior. Incomplete higher-confidence
results may be saved as pending metadata. Use --dry-run for a guaranteed
read-only scan. --auto-import also permits otherwise complete results below the
normal confidence threshold.

Examples:
  # Discover all Git accounts (SSH + GPG)
  gitshift discover

  # Auto-import discovered accounts
  gitshift discover --auto-import

  # Dry run to see what would be discovered
  gitshift discover --dry-run

  # Assign aliases by stable identity (repeat --alias for more accounts)
  gitshift discover --alias 'github|github.com|octocat=personal'

  # Prompt for aliases, accepting a suggestion with Enter
  gitshift discover --prompt-aliases

```
gitshift discover [flags]
```

### Options

```
      --alias stringArray   Set an alias with SELECTOR=ALIAS (repeatable; selector is an identity key or unique suggested alias)
      --auto-import         Also import complete results below the normal confidence threshold
      --dry-run             Show what would be discovered without importing
  -h, --help                help for discover
      --overwrite           Allow discovery even when accounts already exist
      --prompt-aliases      Prompt for aliases not assigned with --alias
```
